articles.title: In 2026, an Oregon teen paid $3.07 for a Lakers jacket at Goodwill; Sotheby’s matched it to Wilt Chamberlain’s 1972 Finals run and sold it for $89,600
articles.summary: International Sports News: A teenager in Oregon bought a warm-up jacket for $3.07 at Goodwill, only to discover it was worn by NBA legend Wilt Chamberlain in the 1972 Finals and sold for an astounding $89,600 at auction.
articles.body: In 2026, a nineteen-year-old reseller bought a warm-up jacket from a Goodwill store near Portland, Oregon, for $3.07; the jacket later turned out to be Wilt Chamberlain's 1972 NBA Finals jacket, authenticated by Sotheby's and sold for $89,600 at auction. This is yet another addition to an ever-growing list of items found in thrift stores that have proven to be significant sports memorabilia.A bargain bin find outside PortlandQuinn Brown, a nineteen-year-old who had been reselling secondhand clothes for three years, was sorting through used clothes at a Goodwill "By-The-Pound" outlet just outside Portland on January 15, 2026, when he noticed a short-sleeved yellow jacket marked "Chamberlain" on the back had been thrown into the bin, according to OPB. He bought the jacket for $3.07 and initially expected to resell it for only a few hundred dollars, as he had found similarly obscure pieces before, according to KPTV. His highest sale to date had been a Sub Pop record-label shirt for $250, reports MyNorthwest. Brown explained that he remembered seeing a Chamberlain warm-up jacket sell for a five-figure sum years earlier, which prompted him to search for pictures of the same jacket online before posting his own find.Verifying a jacket worn by an NBA greatChamberlain, inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1978, is considered to be one of basketball’s all-time dominant players based on statistics from the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. In the Sports Hall of Fame, he continues to break NBA records such as scoring 100 points in one game, grabbing 55 rebounds in one game and averaging 50.4 points per game in the 1961-62 season, all records that have remained untouched for over 60 years. Following Brown's post, Sotheby's experts got in touch with him and managed to convince him to sell the jersey at the auction. Through the use of Sotheby’s photomatching technology, it was concluded that the jersey had been worn by Chamberlain during the finals in the 1971-1972 season when he had defeated the New York Knicks in five games to earn himself the title of the MVP of the finals for the first time in his career.From $3.07 to $89,600 at Sotheby'sSotheby's set the pre-sale estimate at $150,000–$250,000, describing it on their website as an incredible piece of memorabilia. The final bid came way under this estimate, landing at $89,600, including buyer’s premium, after 48 bids had been placed. Even so, the final price was still a remarkable return on the original $3.07 price tag of the jacket, something few pieces bought in thrift stores can compare to.There was, in fact, a significant gap between Sotheby's estimate and the final bid, with the jacket landing $60,400 below the low end of its $150,000-$250,000 range. Such shortfalls aren't unusual for vintage game-worn memorabilia, since matching a piece to a specific game or series through photos alone is difficult. Brown's jacket, however, was one of the rarer pieces for which Sotheby's photomatching technology succeeded in linking it directly to the 1971-72 Finals.A find that stands out even among thrift store discoveriesThe prolific career of Chamberlain ensures that anything having any connection with him will be collected by somebody. He set the NBA record for career rebounds, with a total of 23,924 rebounds, was twice champion, with the Philadelphia 76ers in 1967 and with the Lakers in 1972, and is a four-time MVP, as stated by the California Sports Hall of Fame. In this light, a jacket associated with his championship period holds far more rarity value than mere career memorabilia. For Brown, the sale was the ultimate jump forward in his collecting career, as he moved from a lifetime of making little money by reselling things to selling one thing that made him a huge profit on the $3.07 that he spent. This also shows that sometimes the most valuable sports memorabilia can be found in a donation box somewhere, waiting to be discovered.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: WWE legend Kevin Nash has been in the headlines for his wrestling career and personal life for years. However, in a recent development, the former WWE Champion was accused of one of the most shocking betrayals in life: secretly having an affair with the ex-wife of someone he called a brother for years. That man is none other than his best friend and fellow WWE Hall of Famer, Scott Hall. More shockingly, the accusation came straight from Hall's wife, Dana Hall.Dana Hall accused Kevin Nash of having a secret affair with herIn a recent appearance on Monte and The Pharaoh, Dana Hall made the shocking revelation that she and Kevin Nash had a secret affair behind Scott Hall's back in the late 2000s. Dana said, "This happened in 2008; Kevin was married. Kevin was his best friend. Kevin was the one that’s been shouting from the rooftops that he’s his best friend." She further revealed that the duo hooked up three to four times. "It was like three or four times. I know for three times I can remember for sure, but just, yeah, like booty calls or whatever."However, Dana realized Nash wasn't serious about her after discovering signs that he was hooking up with other women.”I would go there sometimes, and there would be makeup on the pillow from the girl that was before me”, said Dana. At the same time, it is important to note that the secret hookups happened years after Scott Hall and Dana had divorced, first in 1998 and then again in 2001 after they remarried in 1999.WWE Hall of Famers Kevin Nash and Scott Hall formed one of the most iconic factions of all timeKevin Nash and Scott Hall became top WWE superstars during the 1990s and then jumped ship to rival competition, WCW, debuting as 'The Outsiders.' After weeks of teasing a third man to join them, they revealed it to be none other than the ultimate good guy, Hulk Hogan, who turned heel in one of the biggest shockers in professional wrestling. The trio formed the 'nWo' which is considered one of the greatest factions of all time, and Hall and Nash had forged a close bond of friendship.With Nash slapped with these accusations, we will have to wait and see if there will be a public statement released from his side.Also read: 5 WWE superstars who should not win the Money in the Bank 2026 ladder matchGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Caitlin Clark shines, but Fever suffer embarrassing blowout loss to Mystics as playoff race heats up
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark scored 25 points but the Indiana Fever fell 93-77 to the Washington Mystics, slipping behind the Atlanta Dream for fourth seeding.
articles.body: You have to hate Sunday's performance if you're an Indiana Fever fan. The Fever seemed to join Week 2 of the NFL in a scoring slump on Sunday, falling to the Washington Mystics 93-77 in a one-sided loss with real playoff implications on the line. The defeat extinguished much of the Fever's late-season momentum. A squad of Fever veterans got thoroughly outplayed by a youth-heavy Washington roster. (Fever fans, you know how this looks, right? Not great.) THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Caitlin Clark, as expected, led all scorers with 25 points and added five assists, though she also committed five turnovers. Clark and Kelsey Mitchell were the only real sparks for the Fever on Sunday, accounting for 47 of their 77 points. Not even a home-court advantage could elevate the Fever in a miserable all-around outing. The Washington game was crucial for the Fever, who slipped a game behind the Atlanta Dream for fourth seeding. Indiana leaned on the perimeter early, but went 0-for-7 from deep to open the game. Sophie Cunningham, one of the league's top three-point shooters, played just four minutes in the first half as Indiana fell into a 51-30 hole at the break. FEVER COACH STEPHANIE WHITE OPENS UP ABOUT FAN RECEPTION AFTER TURBULENT WEEK OF WNBA CONTROVERSY Washington eventually stretched its lead to 26. Indiana trimmed that deficit to 14 in the third quarter, but that was the best push the Fever could muster against a Mystics team featuring more than half its roster in their first or second year. With two upcoming games against the league-best Minnesota Lynx, the pressure is on coach Stephanie White and the Fever to shake off Sunday's ugly loss and deliver a statement before the postseason. The Fever's first game out of the FIBA break saw them notch an 18-point win over the struggling Toronto Tempo. Sunday's loss wiped away that momentum, but knocking off the Lynx would certainly boost morale in Indy, and then some. articles.title: Once a daily-labourer, fourth-time Asiad campaigner Akash leads Indian squad buoyed by talent pipeline from Manipur
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: KOLKATA: When India men’s sepak takraw captain Akash Yumnam steps onto the court in Nagoya on Monday, it will mark the latest chapter in a journey tha.
articles.body: KOLKATA: When India men’s sepak takraw captain Akash Yumnam steps onto the court in Nagoya on Monday, it will mark the latest chapter in a journey that has taken him from a daily-wage labourer in Manipur to a four-time Asian Games player.The veteran, who used to be a footballer and even spent a month training with NEROCA FC, is set to compete in his fourth Asian Games and remains one of only three members of India’s historic bronze medal-winning men’s regu team from the 2018 Games.But his path to the continental stage was far from straightforward.After losing his father, a government school teacher, in 2013, Akash suddenly found himself responsible for supporting his family. With no steady source of income, he worked as a daily-wage labourer, earning about Rs. 300 a day while continuing to train and pursue his sporting ambitions.“There was a period when I couldn’t even afford coaching expenses. I would work during the day and train in the evenings,” Akash recalled. “My mother, elder brother and younger brother depended on me, so I had to keep going.”The struggles lasted for a couple of years before he was recruited by the Sashastra Seema Bal through the sports quota in 2016. Today, he is not only one of India’s most experienced sepak takraw players but also the leader of a team aiming to return to the Asian Games podium.Akash’s rise mirrors the growth of the sport in Manipur, which continues to serve as the supply line for Indian sepak takraw. Manipur’s influence is evident in India’s Asian Games contingent, with five members of the men’s team and seven from the women’s squad hailing from the state.The state’s dominance was evident at the recent sub-junior nationals in Srinagar, where Manipur won five gold medals and a silver across six events.According to Manipur Sepak Takraw Association general secretary Ch. Geskant, Manipur’s proximity to traditional sepak takraw powerhouses such as Myanmar and Thailand played a key role in the game’s development.The growth has also been sustained by a strong club structure, with organisations such as Laipham Khunou Youth Development Association (LKYDA), Popular Union Club (PUC) and Youth Amateur Welfare Association (YAWA) nurturing generations of players.The state currently has more than 500 registered players, along with nearly 200 players in Under-12 category. The association is active across 13 districts and plans to expand grassroots competitions further.“We are particularly focused on the mini and sub-junior levels because that’s where future talent can be nurtured. There are nearly 200 players in the Under-12 age group and that is one area where we want to focus more attention,” Geskant said.Yet, sepak takraw’s footprint is gradually expanding beyond its northeastern stronghold. One example is Bihar’s Bobby Kumar, the only player from the state in India’s men’s squad. The 20-year-old from Patna discovered the sport at a local park near his home and progressed rapidly through the ranks despite initially knowing little about it.“I never imagined I would play at the Asian Games one day. I started because it looked interesting and gradually fell in love with the game,” he said.Bobby, who recently earned an appointment as a sub-inspector with Bihar Police, was also part of the Indian team that won gold at ISTAF Sepak Takraw World Cup final at Patliputra Sports Complex in Patna last year.India have continued their strong run this year, too, winning the Asian Sepak Takraw Championship title in Nagoya while also claiming a historic World Cup silver in Malaysia and a King’s Cup bronze in Thailand in the Quadrant event.Thanks to these performances, the squad, which has been training intensively in Sonipat for the past two years, is high on confidence ahead of the Asiad, and Akash believes a podium finish is certainly possible.“Our performances over the last two years have been very good. Earlier, we hoped to reach the later stages, but now we truly believe we can win medals,” said the captain.With Akash’s experience, Manipur’s thriving player pipeline and young talents such as Bobby emerging from new centres, India begin their journey in Nagoya with genuine belief that another Asian Games podium finish is within reach.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I did my absolute best': Elavenil’s golden dream falls short, but double silver ends eight-year Asian Games wait
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: The gold was within touching distance — a mere 0.6 points away. But after leading for much of the 10m air rifle final, Elavenil Valarivan, India’s sho.
articles.body: The gold was within touching distance — a mere 0.6 points away. But after leading for much of the 10m air rifle final, Elavenil Valarivan, India’s shooting super star in the making for almost a decade, had to settle for silver.At the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery on a Sunday afternoon, Elavenil provided India’s individual silver lining, while the trio of Elavenil, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod added another silver in the team event.China set a world record of 1904.2 to win the team gold, with India second with 1898, bettering the previous Asian Games record of 1896.6. Hosts Japan took bronze with a score of 1897.1.In the individual final, the 27-year-old made a confident start and, at one stage, held a 1.5-point lead. But as the final entered its business end, the Indian admitted to having “relaxed a bit”, and the gold slipped away.The final was a pulsating affair. Elavenil, who had looked composed throughout, saw her lead disappear late on. With one final shot to come, she produced a 10.1 to finish on 252.4, narrowly missing out on gold. Japan’s Hinata Taichi finished with a flourish, shooting a total of 253 to win the gold and better the Games record of 252.7.Elavenil’s infectious smile wavered briefly. But the overriding expression on her face was relief.After all, these medals had been eight years in the making.If there were nerves, Elavenil did not show them. As she entered the final, she appeared focused and almost oblivious to the competition, which included South Korea’s Olympic and world champion Ban Hyo-jin, who settled for bronze.The teenager who burst onto the scene almost a decade ago has endured more than her share of heartbreak on the biggest stages. Her Asian Games debut in Jakarta in 2018 ended in an anticlimax after a rifle malfunction, while she failed to make the finals at both the Tokyo and Paris Olympics.Those difficult years, she said, were “important for consistency over the years”.On missing out on gold, Elavenil was candid.“I really need to work on my finals more. I knew that I was in the top three. Although I was coming back to focusing on my process and my technique, I did get a bit relaxed. Once the medal was assured, the pressure was released. It was more about me getting a little easy on my process,” she said.“I felt I gave my absolute best and I am glad that it turned out this way,” she added.Elavenil has been on a roll over the past 15 months, with podium finishes at the Asian Championships, World Championships and the Munich World Cup.“I am very grateful that I have been getting many opportunities to learn and experiment and utilise my potential to my absolute best,” she said.As she was being ushered into the press conference, Elavenil pulled out her phone and called her coach Neha Chavan. With the two silver medals around her neck, she flashed her brightest smile.“Ma’am, I just wanted to show the medals to you,” she said.After the press conference, she did the same with her mentor Gagan Narang, who, incidentally, had won silver in the corresponding men’s events at the 2010 Asian Games.Neha may not have been there to watch her climb the podium, but her words stayed with Elavenil.“You have trained your best. There’s nothing more you can do on the day. All I can wish for you is to follow the technique, trust yourself and be courageous, as you have always been,” Neha had told her, Elavenil revealed.Before heading into the final, Elavenil had pulled out her diary. She wrote just one line: “I did my absolute best.”Before she could write more, she was called into the arena.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Neck pillows, no screen time and changing lights: How shooters are tackling conditions at Quaint
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: TimesofIndia in Nagoya: There’s a running joke among members of the Indian shooting contingent that the bus ride from their hotel in central Nagoya to.
articles.body: TimesofIndia in Nagoya: There’s a running joke among members of the Indian shooting contingent that the bus ride from their hotel in central Nagoya to the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery feels like a journey through the bends and turns leading up to Ooty in the Nilgiris.The range, about 75km from their hotel, is the farthest the shooters say, they have had to travel to a venue at an international event. The journey takes close to two hours.“The organisers told us the travel time would be 70 minutes, but it’s about two hours. Given how punctual the Japanese are, we took it at face value. We wish they had told us the actual travel time. We would have been mentally prepared for it,” said Manoj Kumar Ohlyan, chief coach of the 50m rifle team.The shooters, coaches and support staff have since put a few coping mechanisms in place. Most use travel neck pillows to stay comfortable on the winding roads, while screen time is strictly prohibited.“Screen time during such long travel can cause motion sickness, so we tell the shooters they can use their mobiles only to listen to music and not watch anything,” Ohlyan said.Elavenil Valarivan, who suffered a disc bulge in her neck a few years ago, is taking no chances. After winning two silver medals on Sunday, she said, “It’s a long ride to the range and, given my history with the neck, I ensure I travel here with a neck pillow.”The distance, however, is not the only challenge. Ohlyan said the altitude (sitting at an elevation of 670m or nearly 2,200 feet) at the relatively compact range has little bearing on the shooters, but changing light conditions could prove tricky.“The lighting can sometimes be tricky because it is mostly cloudy now. But when there is brighter light, there is a likelihood of a mirage forming when the 50m rifle shooters are in action. So we have discussed the scenarios and made adjustments accordingly,” he said.Team high-performance manager and former shooter Ronak Pandit explained that a change in weather can also affect the shooters psychologically.“Unfortunately, on the day of the match, if we have sunny conditions, the calibration of the rifle changes. Also, here the athletes are trained to shoot in the wind. What could happen is that when you are under pressure and the conditions also go against you, it impacts you psychologically,” Pandit said.“That said, all the shooters are experienced, well-travelled and well-coached. So hopefully, we will be least affected if the conditions change,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: PUNE: Four days ago, when Elavenil Valarivan landed in Japan she carried with her, mixed feelings. The shooter had been to the country before and while that experience may not have been memorable, it was certainly the one to not be forgotten.Elavenil, 27, participated in her first Olympics at Tokyo 2021, where she finished a heartbreaking 16th. While preparing for Aichi-Nagoya, flashes of 2021 returned to her mind, but the shooter, older and wiser now, was able to put them aside.“Thoughts of Tokyo Olympics crossed my mind. It was not a pleasant memory, but over the years, I have trained to put the past behind me and focus on the present. I also told myself that I needed to focus on the Asian Games and not the Olympics,” the shooter told TOI.“I was 22 then and if I had to tell something to my 20-year-old today, I would tell her to be patient and trust the process. I will tell her that the place that gave you heartbreak will also give you a reason to smile about and heal the memories of the past,” she said.‘Ela’ emulated her mentor Gagan Narang, who had also won two silver medals at the 2010 Asian Games. While the mentor was first to call her after her victory, he was also the first to give her some valuable advice. “When I was coming here, he had told me to keep an eye on the weather, the typhoon and plan my bus travels accordingly,” Ela said.In her first Asian Games in 2018, Ela had finished 14th in the same event. The Ahmedabad shooter has been in good form for the past two years and along with the form, other positivity around her has also kept in good shape, mentally. “While on the field, it is the technicality that matters the most. We don’t think about anything that can make us emotional. But off the field, it has been a good phase.”I am happy for my coach Neha (Chavan) ma’am to be nominated for the prestigious Dronacharya Award. She has worked very hard for me, and I am very happy that her efforts have been recognized,” she said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Chess Olympiad Round 5: Praggnanandhaa outwits Dutch No. 1 Anish Giri for first win; Vaishali’s defeat caps India’s mixed day
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: When it was finally revealed that Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa would play Board 1, meaning he would face the toughest oppositions — like his o.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When it was finally revealed that Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa would play Board 1, meaning he would face the toughest oppositions — like his oppoennet in Anish Giri in India's match against the Netherlands on Sunday — at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, many raised eyebrows at world champion Dommaraju Gukesh being pushed down to Board 4, the weakest slot in the line-up. Nobody, though, questioned Praggnanandhaa's credentials to lead the top board.Since an underwhelming campaign at the Cyprus Candidates earlier this year, the Chennai-born grandmaster has been in outstanding form. He beat World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen twice on his way to winning Norway Chess, and last month did something that would have seemed unthinkable a few months earlier, clinching the Grand Chess Tour Finals, becoming only the seventh player, and the first Indian, to do so in the event's 11-year history.His run of late has been so impressive that even five-time world champion Viswanathan Anand, in an interview with TimesofIndia.com, didn't think twice before admitting, "I think at the moment, I would say he's the number one player in the world."After resting on the opening day, a call that saw Arjun Erigaisi step in and lose to lower-rated Thai opponent Prin Laohawirapap, Praggnanandhaa began his Board 1 assignment on Day 2 but managed only three draws across the next three rounds.On Sunday, his opponent was Dutch No. 1, as India were paired against the Netherlands in Round 5.How Praggnanandhaa outsmarted Anish GiriPlaying white, Praggnanandhaa got the better of Giri in a long, grinding game that began as a Ruy Lopez.He built up steady pressure in the centre while Giri took his time working through the middlegame. The position sharpened when Praggnanandhaa allowed his own pawn structure to be damaged in exchange for a tactical shot that won him the exchange, trading a bishop for Giri's rook on b8.Giri fought back with some activity of his own, but Praggnanandhaa's pieces stayed better coordinated throughout.A queen trade led into a tricky rook-and-minor-piece endgame, where Giri's passed pawn on the c-file gave him some practical chances.Praggnanandhaa handled it calmly, using his rook to hunt the pawn down at the right moment and snuff out Black's counterplay for good.From there, his rook and knight took control of the board, with a passed a-pawn adding to the pressure. As Giri's clock ran low, Praggnanandhaa converted the position confidently for his first win of the tournament.Elsewhere, Erigaisi and Nihal Sarin both drew their games, but Gukesh, despite the lower board, beat experienced Erwin L'Ami to help India close out the match 3-1 against the Netherlands.First defeat for the women's team, again against PolandThe picture was far less rosy for India's women, who lost to Poland by a narrow margin, which became India's third straight Olympiad defeat to the Polish side, after losses in 2022 (Chennai) and 2024 (Budapest).The blow fell on Vaishali Rameshbabu, Praggnanandhaa's sister, while the other three boards held to draws.Playing white in a London System, IM Aleksandra Maltsevskaya scored an impressive win over Vaishali.Black accepted a slightly weakened kingside structure early on, then tried to counter by pushing pawns forward aggressively after both sides castled on opposite wings.Maltsevskaya responded, activating her pieces and forcing Vaishali onto the back foot. Her rook barrelled into the seventh rank, and once queens came off the board, her active rooks and advancing pawns proved too much.Vaishali tried to generate some late counterplay with her own rooks, but Maltsevskaya's h-pawn kept marching forward, creating constant promotion threats that eventually broke the position open. Vaishali resigned after 57 moves.With that, India's women slipped to a 1.5-2.5 defeat, with Koneru Humpy, Divya Deshmukh and Vantika Agrawal all drawing their individual games.India will face host Uzbekistan, one of the favourites to win the tournament, on Monday in the open section, while the women's team takes on the USA in what promises to be a fiery clash.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: TimesofIndia in Nagoya: At the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery, Elavenil Valarivan ended a long wait for an Asian Games medal. Some 50km aw.
articles.body: TimesofIndia in Nagoya: At the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery, Elavenil Valarivan ended a long wait for an Asian Games medal. Some 50km away, at the makeshift cricket stadium inside Korogi Sports Park, another delayed milestone was being achieved by prodigal opener Shafali Verma.The Indian opener ended a seven-year wait for a white-ball century on Sunday, smashing an unbeaten 49-ball 100 (3x4, 9x6) to power defending champions India into Tuesday’s final against Sri Lanka.India crushed Bangladesh by 114 runs in a one-sided semifinal after posting 194/4, with Shafali anchoring the innings. Earlier, in a rain-affected semifinal, Sri Lanka eased past Pakistan by eight wickets.Shafali and Smriti Mandhana (37) gave India a flying start with a 72-run opening stand. In the process, Smriti became the highest run-scorer in women’s T20 internationals, taking her tally to 4,788 runs and surpassing New Zealand’s Suzie Bates (4,758).India also had reason to cheer with their captain finding rhythm. Harmanpreet Kaur, who hasn’t had a great run with the bat, struck a 33-ball 40. Bangladesh never threatened in the chase and were bowled out for 81 in 15.4 overs, with Nandini Sharma and Deepti Sharma taking three wickets apiece.For Shafali, though, the afternoon was about finally breaking a barrier that had stood since her T20I debut in 2019. It took her 118 matches to get there.The 22-year-old, who was under the weather, showed no signs of discomfort once she found her rhythm, hitting a boundary and a six off Sanjida Akter in the second over.“This century is very special because from the time I started playing cricket, I’ve manifested scoring a T20 century. I know it took me a long time, but I’m happy that it’s finally come,” a visibly relieved Shafali said.“When I debuted for the team in 2019, I thought T20 was my favourite format and I would put up a show in it, but it took some years for that,” she added.Shafali said she had mixed caution with aggression and rotated the strike, after India’s easy quarterfinal against Japan had left several players short of match practice. “The deliveries which were not in the range, I wanted to play them down. articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: CHENNAI: Indian-origin all-rounder Sabaorish Ravichandran has represented Japan on the global stage for the past four years. But when Japan face India.
articles.body: CHENNAI: Indian-origin all-rounder Sabaorish Ravichandran has represented Japan on the global stage for the past four years. But when Japan face India in a maiden bilateral match ahead of the Asian Games on Tuesday, he will be watching from Chennai.Sabaorish, who recently relocated back home to Chennai, will not be part of Japan’s squad for the historic fixture. He qualifies to play for Japan through residency and has been part of 53 games but, under the Asian Games eligibility rules, needs a Japanese passport to be part of the squad. There is also the practical matter of flying him in for a one-off game.“I have moved back, but I’ll go back to Japan when there’s any tournament. However, bringing me in for just one game (Vs India) would be logistically difficult. Our team is already spending a lot of money to accommodate India there, and our budget is already stretched. We also don’t receive that much funding from the ICC,” Sabaorish, who bats right-handed and bowls leg-spin told TOI.“For the Japan team, this is also preparation for the Asian Games. So they thought it would be better to use the existing Asian Games squad. I’m not part of the Asian Games squad because I don’t possess a Japanese passport,” he added.There was a sense of missing out for Sabaorish, especially because the India-Japan fixture was not something he had seen coming when he decided to move back to Chennai. The discussions about relocating had begun last Sept, and he knew he would miss the Games because of the passport rule. But a bilateral match against India was a different proposition altogether. He admitted he was “really, really down” when the news broke, knowing the occasion could have given him and the Japan team a chance to be noticed.“Sometimes it’s just life, right? Playing against India is like a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity,” said the 34-year-old mechanical engineer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: India’s table tennis campaign at the Asian Games began with contrasting results in the team events, with the women staging a remarkable comeback against Singapore while the men suffered a 0-3 defeat to Iran on Sunday. The Indian women, who had opened their campaign with a 3-0 win over Indonesia, came from 1-2 down to beat Singapore 3-2 in their second Group F tie at the Sky Hall Toyota. Yashaswini Ghorpade and Sreeja Akula held their nerve in the final two matches to seal the victory.India now have four points from their opening two ties and sit atop Group F. Yashaswini had put India ahead with a 3-1 win over Jian Zeng, but Singapore fought back as Sreeja lost a thrilling five-game contest to Ming Loy.Zhao Tan then beat Diya Chitale in four games to put Singapore 2-1 ahead.With India staring at defeat, Sreeja responded emphatically, recovering from losing the opening game 6-11 to beat her opponent 3-1. She won the next three games 11-3, 11-7, 11-4 to level the tie. Yashaswini then returned for the decider and showed considerable composure.After losing the opening game 5-11, she won the next two 11-8, 12-10 before Singapore forced a fifth with an 11-4 win. The final game went down to the wire, but Yashaswini held her nerve to win 11-9 and complete the comeback.Big medal hopes in doublesThe biggest expectations are centred around Manush Shah and Diya Chitale in mixed doubles, while Manav Thakkar and Manush Shah will carry significant hopes in the men’s doubles. articles.body: India’s Suchika Tariyal broke new ground in mixed martial arts at the Asian Games, but the historic moment came with heartbreak. The 36-year-old secured India’s maiden MMA medal at the continental showpiece on Monday, settling for bronze after losing a gruelling women’s traditional 60kg semi-final to Singapore’s Hui Hoon Teo in the extra round.Tariyal went down 0-2 in the extra round after a closely fought contest in which both fighters appeared exhausted, with neither able to land a decisive blow through their punches and kicks. articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India’s Himanshu Dhillon and Rudrankksh Patil added an individual silver and bronze, respectively, to the country’s shooting haul at the Aichi-Nagoya .
articles.body: India’s Himanshu Dhillon and Rudrankksh Patil added an individual silver and bronze, respectively, to the country’s shooting haul at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Monday, capping a memorable morning after the duo had earlier helped India win silver in the men’s 10m air rifle team event.Himanshu held his nerve through the seven-series final to finish second with a score of 252.4, while Rudrankksh ended with 230.9 for bronze. China’s reigning Olympic champion Sheng Lihao won the gold with 254.2, finishing 1.8 points ahead of Himanshu.The two Indians had entered the eight-shooter final after producing strong qualification scores earlier in the morning. Rudrankksh finished third in qualification with 631.8, while Himanshu was seventh with 630.0. Their qualification performances had already secured their places in the individual final and helped India to the team silver.Himanshu started the final strongly, scoring 52.2 in the opening series and moving to 104.8 after two series. He remained in medal contention throughout the elimination phase, eventually finishing second behind Sheng.Rudrankksh, meanwhile, opened with 52.8 and moved into the medal positions early in the final. He remained in the top three through the elimination rounds before finishing with 230.9.The individual medals came just hours after Rudrankksh, Himanshu and Parth Mane combined for 1890.1 points to win silver in the men’s 10m air rifle team event. articles.summary: The Montreal Canadiens acted swiftly during the offseason, signing several of their free agent players to new contracts, including Ivan Demidov, Jakub Dobes,...
articles.body:
The Montreal Canadiens acted swiftly during the offseason, signing several of their free agent players to new contracts, including Ivan Demidov , Jakub Dobes , Alex Newhook , and Arber Xhekaj .

Canadiens fans can rest assured knowing that their window of contention has only just begun opening, as they have several of their key core players under contract for the foreseeable future.

However, Canadiens general manager Kent Hughes could soon have an opportunity to add a proven offensive-minded player who would further boost Montreal's chances of success.

Could The Montreal Canadiens Make A Play For Columbus Blue Jackets Forward Kirill Marchenko ?

The Blue Jackets have had to face uncomfortable questions about two different key players in recent months, starting with the future of Norris Trophy winning defenseman Zach Werenski , along with former 74-point forward Kirill Marchenko.

Additionally, top forward Adam Fantilli has yet to report to Camp, adding another layer of uncertainty to the upcoming season in Columbus.

Marchenko, who is entering the final year of his current contract, didn't exactly make it sound like he was itching to sign a long-term extension in Columbus during a recent interview at Blue Jackets Training Camp.

"I can talk only about hockey," Marchenko said when asked about his contract status. "It's not my side, [the] business side. It's on [Blue Jackets president/general manager Don Waddell] and Dan [Milstein], and they [will] figure out everything. My goal [is] to be ready, on the ice."

"It's too many good questions right now," he continued. "I want to play hockey. That's what I can say right now, and I don't want to give you guys a lot of things. I just love [my] teammates, I love to enjoy the practices and enjoy the hockey. It's my favorite thing in the world, and I just do my job."

Entering the final year of his deal before he's eligible to become a restricted free agent, Marchenko's salary cap hit for 2026-27 is $3,850,000.

Kirill Marchenko Has Played His Entire NHL Career With The Blue Jackets

Marchenko was taken by the Blue Jackets in the second round (49th overall pick) of the 2018 NHL Draft, and he began his North American career with the American Hockey League affiliate Cleveland Monsters. After registering an impressive 19 points in 16 games, he earned his first NHL call-up in December 2022.

He would score his first NHL goal in his fourth game and later became the first rookie that season to record a hat trick. Marchenko continued to produce throughout his debut campaign, finishing with 21 goals and setting a Blue Jackets new rookie record for goals.

He added another natural hat trick against Buffalo in December 2023 before signing a three-year, $11.55 million contract with Columbus in July 2024. It was in the 2024-25 NHL season that he reached a career-best 74 points, scoring 31 goals with 43 assists.

That number dipped slightly to 67 points last season, as he tallied 27 goals with 40 assists in 76 games played.

So far in his NHL career, Marchenko has scored 102 goals with 106 assists in 292 games. But he's still waiting to appear in his first Stanley Cup Playoff action.

articles.title: Studs and duds from Colts' Week 2 overtime loss vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: Let's take a look back at the Colts' Week 2 performance with the studs and duds from the team's overtime loss to the Chiefs.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts fell just short in overtime to the Kansas City Chiefs . With this loss, the Colts find themselves 0-2 and on a nine-game losing streak dating back to last season.

Looking back at Sunday's game, here are the studs and duds from the Colts' performance.

As he often does, Taylor shouldered the workload on offense. In a game where the Colts totaled 329 yards, Taylor accounted for 132 of those yards. He ran for 92 yards and was also involved in the passing game with four receptions for 40 more yards. He also scored two touchdowns.

Indianapolis generated two sacks and four quarterback hits. Mahomes was pressured on just 22.4% of his dropbacks. The Colts' ability to get after the quarterback was a question mark coming into the season, and through two games it remains one.

There were a lot more short-to-intermediate throws in this game, which was perhaps a product of not having Alec Pierce for much of the game, and Ashton Dulin being ruled out on Friday. But in their absence, Josh Downs provided a go-to presence for Daniel Jones , which he often does. Downs caught 7-of-9 passes for 72 yards -- leading the team in all three categories.

The defense is nowhere near good enough. That's a roster-construction issue, and that ultimately falls on the play caller. The Colts again surrendered over 500 yards of offense. Patrick Mahomes was both efficient and generated chunk plays, while the Chiefs' run game averaged over five yards per carry as a team. There are holes throughout this unit, and it's making things quite difficult for the Colts' own offense.

Shrader was perfect on the night, making all three extra point attempts and all three field goals. This included making a game-tying extra point and a game-tying field goal in the fourth quarter and overtime.

articles.title: Titans Star Jeffery Simmons Goes Viral for Wild Eagles Fan Taunt Before Late Collapse
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans looked like they were seconds away from celebrating a statement upset over the Philadelphia Eagles, and star defensive tackle Jeffery Si...
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans looked like they were seconds away from celebrating a statement upset over the Philadelphia Eagles, and star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons was clearly enjoying the moment. Tennessee grabbed a late fourth-quarter lead, putting Philadelphia in danger of leaving Nashville with a loss.

Then a video involving Simmons began spreading across social media and added another layer to an already heated matchup.

The clip appeared to show Simmons directing an obscene gesture and vulgar message toward Eagles fans in the crowd while Tennessee held the late advantage. Heavy will not repeat the language or describe the gesture in explicit detail, but the message was clear (video here). Simmons appeared more than ready to let Philadelphia fans hear about it while the Titans were in position to finish the upset.

Titans' Jeffery Simmons Had Been Talking All Week

The moment gained even more attention because Simmons had already become one of the central personalities surrounding Eagles-Titans.

He had been outspoken leading into the matchup, particularly while discussing Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts and how Tennessee planned to defend him. That made Simmons an easy target for Eagles fans once the game eventually flipped.

Simmons also gave himself plenty of reason to be confident during the game. Tennessee pushed Philadelphia deep into the fourth quarter and briefly appeared ready to finish off one of the weekend's more notable upsets.

When the Titans grabbed the late lead, Simmons appeared to turn his attention toward the visiting fans and celebrate accordingly. There was only one problem. The game was not over.

Eagles Made Viral Simmons Moment Age Quickly

Philadelphia responded after Tennessee's late score and ultimately escaped with the victory, completely changing how Simmons' celebration looked only minutes later.

What could have become a viral clip attached to a Titans upset instead became immediate ammunition for Eagles fans across social media. Few things age faster in professional sports than a celebration that happens before the final whistle.

That does not erase how well Tennessee competed or how disruptive Simmons can be when he is at his best. It does, however, create the kind of sequence the internet rarely lets disappear quietly. Simmons appeared ready to celebrate directly in front of Philadelphia's traveling fan base, only to watch the Eagles snatch the game back before Tennessee could finish the job.

The story also fits the tone surrounding Simmons all week. He talked before the matchup, played with plenty of emotion and appeared to have even more to say when Tennessee moved ahead late. None of that is unusual for one of the NFL's most intense defensive stars, but the timing made this particular moment impossible to ignore. The Titans nearly had the upset. Simmons nearly had the last word. Philadelphia made sure he did not.

articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs survived a grueling 33-30 brawl against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night, grinding out a victory that went straight down to the final second of overtime. Harrison Butker predictably split the uprights to give KC a 30-27 lead in extra time, but Indy stubbornly refused to throw in the towel. For a tame four quarters, action rocketed in overtime, notably when Colts QB Daniel Jones connected with Laquon Treadwell on a 48-yard bomb deep into Chiefs territory, setting up a game-tying field goal by Spencer Shrader to make it 30-30. Yes, Laquon Treadwell, of all people — the former Vikings first-rounder out of Ole Miss who never lived up to his draft slot. Butker ended the chaos on the following drive, drilling a 40-yard game-winner as time expired in extra time. Following the loss, Daniel Jones fell to an abysmal 1-16 in career primetime starts, and he hasn't tasted a night-game victory since 2022 when he played for New York. Kansas City couldn't put away the Colts with ease, but they found a way. While Indianapolis searches for answers in 2026, Kansas City is proving the dynasty magic remains very much intact. Patrick Mahomes carved up Indy, completing 32-of-47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns. Hand-wringing over his mobility headlined the opener against Denver, but Mahomes proved he can dismantle a secondary strictly from the pocket. "We didn't do exactly what we wanted to do," Mahomes said postgame, while lauding his team's resilience. COLTS FACE QUARTERBACK UNCERTAINTY AS DANIEL JONES RECOVERS FROM ACHILLES INJURY Across the sideline, Jones posted an efficient line in defeat for Indy, finishing 22-of-31 for 210 yards, one touchdown and an interception. Targeting Travis Kelce early and often paid dividends, as the veteran tight end poured in nine catches for 101 yards and a touchdown for KC. Kenneth Walker III chewed up turf on the ground, rushing 24 times for 117 yards. Naturally, Taylor Swift was in the suite alongside her mother, Andrea, and set the internet on fire by flashing her ring after Kelce scored Kansas City's first touchdown. Jonathan Taylor was an absolute workhorse for Indianapolis, proving impervious to Steve Spagnuolo’s defense while racking up 132 total yards (92 rushing on 24 carries, four catches for 40 yards) and two touchdowns. articles.title: Mahomes Leads Chiefs to Wild Overtime Win Over Colts
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are 2-0, but they certainly had to earn it. Kansas City survived a wild Sunday night battle with the Indianapolis Colts, escaping Arro...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 2-0, but they certainly had to earn it.

Kansas City survived a wild Sunday night battle with the Indianapolis Colts , escaping Arrowhead Stadium with a 33-30 overtime victory. The win keeps the Chiefs unbeaten to start the season, while Indianapolis falls to 0-2.

Patrick Mahomes was outstanding throughout the night. The Chiefs quarterback completed 32 of 47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception. After a somewhat uneven opening game, Mahomes looked much more comfortable and aggressive against Indianapolis.

Travis Kelce was once again a major part of the offense. Kelce caught nine passes for 101 yards and a touchdown, giving Mahomes a reliable target throughout the night. Tyquan Thornton also made several explosive plays, finishing with 86 receiving yards.

Kansas City built a 27-20 lead in the fourth quarter, but the Colts refused to go away.

Jonathan Taylor scored his second rushing touchdown of the game with just over five minutes remaining, tying the game at 27-27 and eventually sending the matchup into overtime.

Both teams traded field goals in overtime before Mahomes got the ball back with a chance to finish the game.

Mahomes connected with Kenneth Walker III for a 22-yard completion that moved the Chiefs deep into Indianapolis territory. Walker also finished with 117 rushing yards, giving Kansas City another major weapon on a night when the offense produced 523 total yards.

That set up Harrison Butker for the final moment.

Butker drilled a 40-yard field goal as time expired, sending Arrowhead into a frenzy and giving Kansas City the 33-30 victory.

The Chiefs aren't perfect, but they are 2-0, and Mahomes appears to be finding his rhythm quickly. After missing much of last season with a major knee injury, his performance Sunday night was another encouraging sign for Kansas City.

The Chiefs will now head into Week 3 unbeaten, with Mahomes and the offense looking increasingly dangerous.

articles.title: Why Alec Pierce Isn’t Playing for Colts vs. Chiefs With Injury News
articles.summary: Alec Pierce started Sunday Night Football for the Indianapolis Colts. He won’t finish it, though, as the Colts lose their most explosive offensive weapon aga...
articles.body:
Alec Pierce started Sunday Night Football for the Indianapolis Colts .

He won't finish it, though, as the Colts lose their most explosive offensive weapon against the Kansas City Chiefs .

Pierce was injured in the first half, on a play where he didn't even get the ball.

As things developed, Pierce was first ruled as questionable to return. He was eventually ruled out.

Pierce was ruled out with a heel injury.

It was to the same left heel that he had surgery on during the offseason.

NBC sideline reporter Melissa Stark reported that Pierce had gone to the locker room for X-rays, and it wasn't long after that that he was ruled out.

Pierce appeared to get injured making a cut on a route, and he limped to the sideline and went with trainers straight to the blue medical tent.

He was in the tent between 5-10 minutes, then rode on the cart to the locker room.

Pierce was originally not certain to be ready for Week 1 after his offseason surgery, but he made it back in time.

Against the Baltimore Ravens in the opener, Pierce had four catches for 61 yards.

He had limited snaps in that game, but he was probably full bore in Week 2 before he got hurt.

The Colts don't have a particularly deep wide receiver depth chart, particularly with one injury already on the books heading into Week 2.

They have the smaller Josh Downs , who is reliable but nothing like Pierce. He mostly works out of the slot.

On the outside, they'll likely have to use Laquon Treadwell a lot more. He's the former first-round pick who is now a journeyman

The Colts also have the veteran Keenan Allen , who is still playing while awaiting for potential suspension news from the NFL — which might not come for another month or more.

Beyond that, there's the speedy rookie Deion Burks , and the elevated-this-week Anthony Gould , who is playing in place of the injured Ashton Dulin .

They're certainly worse without Pierce. He led the NFL in yards per catch in 2025. This injury could change his chances of doing that in 2026.

articles.title: Commanders news: Gruesome Jayden Daniels injury had Rachaad White literally in tears
articles.summary: Rachaad White has known Jayden Daniels far longer than their time together in Washington, which made Sunday harder to watch than most. The Commanders running...
articles.body:
Rachaad White has known Jayden Daniels far longer than their time together in Washington , which made Sunday harder to watch than most. The Commanders running back, who played alongside Daniels at Arizona State, admitted he broke down after the quarterback dislocated his left elbow in a 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium.

"I tried to, you know, control my emotions, 'cause yeah, I mean, I had tears coming down," White told reporters after the game . "I feel for him. That's my brother."

White was part of the play itself. On the final snap of the first half, with Washington mere feet from the Dallas goal line, Daniels' feet tangled with the cleats of left guard Chris Paul . He stumbled backward and extended his left arm to brace himself, and the elbow gave way. Daniels still tried to finish the play, flipping a shovel pass toward White that fell incomplete, before walking toward the sideline and collapsing to the turf.

He was carted to the locker room and ruled out. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed the dislocation afterward , adding that X-rays showed no fracture. Daniels is scheduled for more imaging Monday.

The injury is to the same left elbow Daniels dislocated in Week 9 last season against Seattle , a setback that cost him three games before he aggravated it again in December and was shut down. He played just seven games in 2025, and Sunday was only his second game back.

The emotional toll spread through the locker room . Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota , who is set to start in Daniels' place, felt it as much as anyone. "It sucks, and you can't even really put it into words," he said. "You watch that kid battle through all that he went through last year." He was the first player to reach Daniels on the field.

Daniels emerged from the locker room after the game with his left arm in a sling, walking to where family and friends were waiting and sharing hugs before leaving.

Quinn made clear how Washington intends to respond. "We will rally so hard around Marcus until Jayden is back," he said. "That's what's required, and that's what we'll do." The Commanders, now 0-2, host the Seattle Seahawks next Sunday with Mariota under center.

The Indianapolis Colts received a crucial initial sigh of relief during Sunday night's Week 2 showdown against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. Wide receiver Alec Pierce exited early in the contest with a left heel injury. The initial X-rays came back negative , according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Pierce pulled up awkwardly while running a route, hopped off the turf unable to put weight on his left leg, and was examined in the medical tent before being carted to the locker room. Prior to his exit, he logged one reception for 11 yards.

The concern is heightened because Pierce underwent an offseason procedure on the same left ankle and heel area earlier this year. That delayed his offseason participation. With Indianapolis preparing for a Week 3 AFC South matchup against Houston , the Colts will wait for Monday's tests to determine whether Pierce avoided a more significant soft-tissue issue.

articles.title: Son honors late father with special yellow-haired hats for Chiefs game
articles.summary: A lot of people at Sunday night's Chiefs game against the Colts were wearing red Chiefs hats. However, that's not the case for Cole and Kayla Henry and all t...
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY — A lot of people at Sunday night's Chiefs game against the Colts were wearing red Chiefs hats. However, that's not the case for Cole and Kayla Henry and all their friends.

Jack Henry was a retired Kansas City police officer of 25 years. He also was a die-hard Chiefs fans and season ticket holder since 1994. Instead of wearing just any ordinary hats or outfits on game day, he would always look to go the extra yard.

"Anytime my dad was on vacation, he was always constantly looking for anything Chiefs-related, so when he saw some of these hats in Mexico that had the spiky yellow hair, he's like, 'Oh, I can wear that to the Chiefs game,'" Colt Henry, Jack's son, said.

Unfortunately, Jack Henry passed away from cancer in hospice care on Thursday. To honor him and his traditions, Colt Henry, his wife Kayla Henry and a group of their friends are taking one out of his playbook.

"My buddies here decided to do a little ode to my dad," Colt said. "As a matter of fact, that's where the number here kind of comes from, is the 94. This is one of the season ticket members' gifts that the Chiefs gave him. So, yeah, we're just kind of showing a little respect in memory to him."

While Jack Henry isn't at Sunday night's game physically, he's still watching the Chiefs take the field spiritually. He even gets a seat right next to his son and daughter-in-law.

"We have his seat ticket today and didn't sell it, brought his jersey to hang over it [the seat] for the game," Kayla Henry, Jack Henry's daughter-in-law, said.

Now, Colt looks to take on the yellow, spiky-haired hat tradition for years to come.

"I know for him, there was a level of comfort knowing that he was going to pass along kind of the traditions and everything to me, and that maybe I would take the helm of everything he kind of started," Colt said.

Colt tells FOX4 he was able to watch the Chiefs play with his dad one last time during Monday Night Football, when they beat the Broncos 31-10.

articles.title: Carrick confident Man Utd can turn form around after Fulham draw
articles.summary: Michael Carrick remains convinced Manchester United can enjoy a successful season despite another frustrating result, insisting the team’s recent run has bee...
articles.body:
Michael Carrick remains convinced Manchester United can enjoy a successful season despite another frustrating result, insisting the team's recent run has been made to look worse by a series of fine margins.

United were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham at Craven Cottage, with Lisandro Martinez 's own goal putting the hosts ahead before Matheus Cunha's late deflected effort rescued a point for the visitors.

Carrick was frustrated by the result, particularly after United created enough chances to take all three points. Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno was named his side's standout performer, while United also struck the post twice.

"We are not happy about not winning the game but there are things to take from this game, for sure," Carrick told MUTV and Sky Sports.

The United head coach believes his team's response after falling behind was particularly encouraging, with the players continuing to attack and eventually finding a way back into the game.

"The way we responded to going down was really pleasing," he said. "The boys were really positive and played with good purpose."

Carrick also pointed to several unfortunate moments that have contributed to United dropping points, including the late Everton goal, Manchester City 's controversial goal and Martinez's own goal at Fulham.

He stressed, however, that United cannot allow those incidents to distract from areas where improvement is required.

"There are parts we can do better," Carrick admitted. "We need to learn a lot from this first chapter of the season really and we need to be better, that is pretty clear."

The draw came as United began a lengthy break from club football, giving Carrick time to reflect on the opening part of the campaign before his players return from international duty.

The manager believes the upcoming run of fixtures will provide an important opportunity for his squad to build momentum.

"This first chapter feels a bit of a sprint," Carrick said. "We wanted more points, we haven't quite got them, but there's still a lot of encouragement from me moving forward."

Despite the disappointment, Carrick remains confident about what lies ahead.

"I'm convinced we'll have a good season," he said. "We're having a spell that feels bigger than it actually is to the outside. We'll get back to winning football matches and we'll be alright."

For now, United head into the international break with work still to do, but Carrick believes the performance at Fulham offered enough encouragement to suggest the situation can change quickly.

articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. quiet when Arizona Cardinals need him most
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. finished without a reception in the Arizona Cardinals' loss to the Seattle Seahawks. He has one catch on four targets this season.
articles.body:
By the time reporters entered the Arizona Cardinals locker room, Marvin Harrison Jr. was gone.

His cream-toned rivalry-edition helmet hung from one hook. A few pieces of his discarded uniform hung from another. His black shoes sat on the ground, a green energy drink on a shelf. This was all the evidence that Harrison had been there at all.

In a 31-7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , Harrison ran 31 routes and saw one target, by the official definition. Even that is generous. The pass was effectively a throwaway, spiked incomplete at Harrison's feet.

Arizona Cardinals' 2026 home opener vs. Seattle Seahawks in photos

And so, for the first time in the career of the 2024 No. 4 overall draft pick, he finished a healthy game with zero receptions.

Entering this season, Harrison had an opportunity in front of him, with a new coaching staff and a new starting quarterback. He had proven inconsistent across his first two seasons, averaging just 51.5 yards per game and topping 75 yards on just five occasions. But perhaps the issue was his rapport with Kyler Murray , or his usage in Drew Petzing's scheme.

Then, in Week 1, Harrison finished with one catch on three targets. So after a silent Week 2, he has now run 68 routes this season, earned four targets and hauled in just one reception.

Over the past decade, 12 wide receivers have been selected inside the top 10 of the NFL draft. Analyzing the first three seasons for each, only three of those players have produced a two-game stretch with one reception or fewer: Mike Williams , John Ross and now Harrison.

In his postgame press conference, head coach Mike LaFleur played down Harrison's slow start.

"I wouldn't look into too much of anything right now," LaFleur said. "Because we didn't throw the ball for crap anyway. Schematically, it wasn't good."

Similarly, quarterback Jacoby Brissett attributed Harrison's struggles to Seattle's defensive discipline.

"They stay in the structure of staying two-high," Brissett said. "It's kind of hard to push the ball. It was hard to find completions today."

Indeed, the Cardinals managed just 95 passing yards, their fewest in a game since a shutout loss to Cleveland in 2023. But Harrison was drafted to be the type of player who they could look to in difficult moments, to provide an outlet when no one else could.

Instead, the offense ran through everyone else. Trey McBride caught eight of his 10 targets. Michael Wilson caught just two of his seven, but he drew a pair of pass interference penalties to move the chains. Even Kendrick Bourne , Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier saw multiple targets.

Harrison, meanwhile, was rarely used. Even when Brissett did look Harrison's way, it seemed as if a Seahawks cornerback was always glued to his hip.

It's not just the statistical production. In his first two seasons, Harrison played 83% and 86% of offensive snaps, excluding games he exited due to injury. So far this season, his snap share has dipped to just 77%.

Against the Seahawks, Harrison was on the field for 74% of offensive plays, a number that was even lower before the Cardinals began playing catch-up late in the second half.

Targets can be fluky, but snap share is a coach's decision, earned by what players show on the practice field.

"Some of it was being in 13 (personnel) big," LaFleur said. "So you only end up having one receiver in there. We were in what we call 13 Z, and that's where Mike's our receiver in that. When we're in 13 X, which we had a couple snaps of that, Marv's our receiver in that."

LaFleur was then asked whether he is concerned with Harrison's performance through two games. He paused before answering.

"Not concerned, no," LaFleur said. "I'm concerned with, obviously, our execution on offense today."

This remains the public line when those inside the organization are asked about Harrison.

Earlier this week, wide receivers coach Tony Sorrentino pointed to Harrison's intelligence and said he is "excited about him getting better and better every single day."

In the postgame locker room, left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. said Harrison has the same mentality he did at Ohio State, where the two were college teammates.

"He's one of the greatest receivers I've seen with my own two eyes," Johnson said. "I believe anybody that doesn't see that, I don't think they know football."

But as the defense of Harrison grows louder, the results grow quieter. Entering Monday Night Football, he ranks 142nd in the NFL in receiving yards.

And against the Seahawks, when the Cardinals needed someone to drag them out of an offensive quagmire, Harrison produced the worst statistical game of his career.

"It's frustrating for sure," Brissett said. "I'm sure it's frustrating for him; it's also frustrating for me. But it's Week 2."
