articles.title: Home Team Friday Week 6 “Power 10”
articles.summary: HENDERSON, Ky. (WEHT) – Each week, the Tri-State shows off some of the most talented high school football teams in their respective states. But how do fans k...
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Ky. (WEHT) – Each week, the Tri-State shows off some of the most talented high school football teams in their respective states. But how do fans know who is the best of the best when the lights turn on Friday night? That's where the Home Team Friday "Power 10" comes into play.

Our expert sports team is constantly studying dozens of teams each week to create a top-10. Wins, losses, injuries, strength of schedule and margin of victory/defeat are all factors in the decision-making process.

Here are the Week 5 "Power 10" rankings:

Just like the weather on Friday night, it took the Aces some time to get right. Bardstown went 70 yards on the opening drive. Then scored again following a 45-minute lighting delay. Friday night was also a reminder that the Aces star Dre'Mail Carothers is human as he threw two interceptions against the Tigers. But despite all of that, O Cath stayed calm and climbed back for a 12-0 deficit and scored 49 unanswered points as they rolled past Bardstown 49-12. Obviously, a slow start wasn't what the Aces wanted, but they didn't blink when adversity came which speaks to the maturity of this group. The defense looked good once again giving up 12 points or fewer for the second straight week. Owensboro Catholic stays at the top and will remain there as long as they keep winning in dominant fashion. Next for them is a battle vs Meade Co. at home on Friday.

Weather was a problem all around the tri-state and no one was impacted by it more than the Tigers. Memorial's matchup vs Harrison at Romain Stadium didn't kick off till nearly 9 p.m. The long delay didn't cause any performance issues for the Tigers though as they crushed the Warriors 52-20. The Tigers offense got hot from the opening possession as they scored on the opening drive. Then it was the defenses turn as senior LB Grayson Carter ran home a pick-6 which made it a 14-0 first quarter start for Memorial. Gene Aimone was the standout player for the Tigers as he finished the contest with 8 carries, 109 rushing yards and one score. Like they usually do, the Tigers handled business and didn't play down to a Warriors team they were expected to beat easily. The unbeaten record stays intact as Memorial prepared for a home game vs Bosse on Friday.

This should come as a surprise to no one; the Titans topped 30 points again for in week five and kept the streak alive. Peyton Johnson also recorded his fifth straight game with over 100 receiving yards (9 receptions, 144 receiving yards, 1TD). The week four Home Team Friday MVP has been simply unstoppable this season along with his buddy Caden Rochleau (279 passing yards, 3TD's). The senior duo is arguably the best in the entire tri-state area, and they have their Titans playing incredible football going into week six. In case you were wondering what they final score was, they beat Southridge 43-21. The only question that remains for this team is their defenses ability to limit points against the good teams. That will be tested in week six as they face a very good Heritage Hills team in Lincoln City.

The Red Devils needed some positives after a tough road loss to Owensboro Catholic and they got that as they throttled Graves Co. in Rash Stadium. Owensboro's defense reminded everyone that they are still among the best in Kentucky as they held the Eagles to just 7 points on their way to a 49-7 win. With some injuries still lingering for the team, big stars are needed and no one played better than their star LB Ty Ashley. The senior had two rushing and one passing touchdown on offense and contributed a handful of tackles on defense as well. The Red Devils have been in this situation before with a 3-2 record entering week six last season, and they won it all. So it isn't crazy to think this team can still find themselves at the top at years end. In other great news, this team is also nearing the return timeline of QB Damaracus Ganaway Jr. Owensboro is still unbeaten at home this season and they look keep that streak alive against Apollo on Friday.

There is a 1A and 1B in the Southern Indiana Athletic Conference, and it's Memorial and Reitz. The Panthers proved once again that they deserve to be talked about as one of the conferences best as they easily beat Central 61-13. RB Amyr Wilford was talked about in high regard this offseason, but I don't think anyone could have predicted this level of excellence from sophomore. On Friday he passed his freshman year mark of 13 rush touchdowns... in just five games. Wilford went for 267 rushing yards and 5 TD scores in just the first half and now has 14 touchdowns on the season. It is safe to say he has put himself on the map as one of Indiana's best running backs. The Panthers welcome a very good Castle team to the Reitz Bowl on Friday.

The Vikings stay perfect and beat Pike Central by a lot 58-0. North Posey's defense was the highlight of the night as they pitched their first shutout of the season. It is hard to imagine a 5-0 team ranked #6 in the "Power 10" but it just proves how stacked the talent pool is in the tri-state. Regardless of the ranking; just know that the Vikings are a great team and look like a threat to anyone they play. Their red-hot offense rolls into South Spencer on Friday as they look to stay perfect.

Just like the Red Devils, this Apollo team is a very good 3-2 team and their offense is one of the best in the "Power 10." A long ride to Muhlenberg Co. didn't stop QB Max Johnson from continuing his hot streak either. The senior now has over one thousand passing yards to go along with 20 pass touchdowns and just one interception this year. There is a reason why he will be a D1 quarterback next fall. Last Friday also served as a needed momentum boost for this Apollo defense which allowed their few points on season so far in a 34-7 victory. Week six will be another great one in Owensboro as they Eagles take on the Red Devils.

In case anyone was wondering, the Pats are still a very.. very good team and remain a strong force in the tri-state football scene. Coach Kevin Temple has this team firing on all cylinders as Heritage Hills walked to a 59-0 road win over Washington. The offense has scored 40 points or more in four out of five weeks and the defense has been phenomenal as well. The Patriots have scored 169 points in the last three weeks and given up 0. That is getting it done. Everyone talked about the expected drop off of this team going into the year, which was expected with their key departures, but the Pats have proven that they aren't going anywhere. Their biggest test of the season comes this week as they face a great Gibson Southern squad in Lincoln City.

The head coaching job of Cody Hess in year two has been flat out impressive as the young Wildcats stretch their record to three games over .500. A slow start to the season hurt Mater Dei last year, but that hasn't happened in 2026. Mater Dei is clearly a strong football team and one of the SIAC's best, which carries some weight when you look at the strength of the conference. Their 16-13 road win over Jasper proved yet again that the Wildcats can win games in a multitude of ways as their defense played great all night. Mater Dei has yet to give up more than 20 points in games they have won this year. It is no time to rest though, and their head coach will tell you that, because another test awaits them Friday as they play North on the road.

The Knights have now run off three wins in a row since their week two loss to Mater Dei. It is beginning to feel like Castle will be a very good team that hangs it this season and could be capable of beating anyone on a Friday night. Statements were made as they ran over Boonville 34-6 last Friday and looked awesome on offense. Javion Aunspach played his way into a week 5 HTF MVP nomination with 8 receptions, 112 receiving yards, and 1 TD. Senior WR Ben Quach, who is recently back from injury, got in on the scoring as well with a long TD reception in the first quarter. Brodie Farmer continues to lead these Knights with his 10 tackles against the Pioneers. Injuries hindered the Knights in a big way last season, but that hasn't been an issue yet in 2026 and Castle is thriving because of it. Week six is a huge test as they take on Reitz.

Just missed the cut: Mt. Carmel (Mount Carmel, Il), Madisonville-North Hopkins (Madisonville, Ky) Boonville (Boonville, Ind.)

A new ranking will be released at the beginning of each week throughout football season until the playoffs begin

articles.title: Renee Slegers’ Arsenal are a team weighed down by a debilitating lack of urgency
articles.summary: Renee Slegers wastes no time. The Arsenal Women head coach gets in there, remonstrating at the fourth official. Goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez is squaring up to t...
articles.body:
Renee Slegers wastes no time. The Arsenal Women head coach gets in there, remonstrating at the fourth official. Goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez is squaring up to the referee. And really, who could blame them?

The final whistle has gone and who will speak up for the seconds not added on after Smilla Holmberg's last-gasp equalising goal against Manchester United in the fifth minute of six added on? Or the seconds lost to United goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce failing to register the urgency of the moment as Arsenal try to avoid dropping any more points inside their first three league matches of the season? Who will speak up for those precious opportunities lost in battle, if not them?

Of course, there were plenty of opportunities before those to see off then-bottom-of-the-table and point-less Manchester United: any of the prior 94 minutes (5,640 seconds) in fact. Not that such facts halted Slegers from radiating a kind of wounded sincerity as she assessed her team's 1-1 draw with United, Arsenal's second stalemate in as many matches following their goalless draw with Crystal Palace last weekend, another two points dropped from a possible nine in their opening three Women's Super League (WSL) matches.

Turn it one way and Holmberg's late equaliser represented a kind of salvation. Arsenal had been well on their way to scuppering claims to a club-record 20-match unbeaten run in the WSL, a seventh-successive WSL match unbeaten against United, thanks to Julia Zigiotti Olme 's opener in the 67th minute following miscommunication between Steph Catley and Georgia Stanway . That was until Leah Williamson found her Swedish team-mate blitzing in at the back post at the death, one of 17 shots to, finally, cushion the netting with 60 seconds of stoppage time to spare.

Displeasure rang out among the home crowd as the full-time whistle sounded. Amid the boos, of course, were also sighs, head shakes, and despondent mutterings of inevitabilities. Because the human construct of time is as compelling a scapegoat as any but those watching know the familiar feeling of an opportunity dropped.

Before Saturday, United head coach Eva Olid insisted, despite two league defeats, seven goals conceded and a rock-bottom berth, she didn't want to compromise too greatly on her desire to play attacking football, the task assigned her upon her appointment last month .

Yet, a pretty dependable blueprint for taking points off Arsenal has come to cement itself as a tempting venture even to the most zealous of ideologues. Ask newly-promoted Crystal Palace. Or Brighton & Hove Albion from last season. Or Aston Villa . Or Tottenham Hotspur . Make Arsenal pry you open. Ask them to puncture you. Because if you face Arsenal but defend in a mid-to-low block, did you even really play Arsenal?

That existential question has plagued this pocket of north London for the past few seasons. Of course, the more pressing issue is what this draw with United actually means. No one should leap too far. There are 26 league games to play. Three have transpired. The WSL title race is a marathon, not a sprint. And while reigning champions Manchester City have yet to drop points this season and Chelsea dispatched United with the kind of ease reserved for pre-season last time out, the competitive levels of the WSL are once again at their highest, meaning the likelihood of Chelsea or City failing to drop points from this point onwards is negligible.

And still, this compulsive twitch of Arsenal's to draw, for shared spoils, for final-third profligacy and sporadic but ultimately belated surges of urgency, has become their own silent stumbling block.

Last season, Arsenal suffered just one league defeat, their fewest since the 2021-22 campaign. Yet, they drew on six occasions, a total of 12 points dropped, a club-record high. City, meanwhile, lost three times but drew just once. Chelsea drew four times. In fact, Arsenal's six draws were the second-most in the league behind United.

Consistency in the final third has represented a recurring problem area under Slegers, particularly when met with mid-to-low blocks. Last season, Arsenal finished the WSL campaign having surpassed their xG by +4.6, a league high. Following Saturday's draw, Arsenal have scored just twice from 60 shots this campaign. They have fallen short of their xG (5.9) by -3.9, the greatest disparity in the league.

In their goalless draw with Palace, Arsenal had 70 touches in Palace's final third, the most by a team without scoring in a WSL game since April 2018 when Arsenal themselves failed to score against Yeovil Town. Against United, Arsenal registered 59 touches in the final third, as well as four big chances and 17 shots in total. By contrast, United registered three touches in Arsenal's final third, the same number as their total shots on target.

Holding Slegers solely liable for her team's poor conversion rates and decision-making in the final third would be misleading. The likelihood that chances will, eventually, be converted is high.

Yet questions can be asked of why Alessia Russo — Arsenal's top goalscorer last season with 13 goals and the team's nominal No 9 — remains marooned as a No 10 despite myriad windows to pick up an actual No 10.

Or whether Russo's ability to receive the ball with her back to goal outweighs her ability to do much with it when she does.

Or the value of Ona Batlle , a right-back, playing on the left.

Or why Arsenal have spent successive recruitment windows bringing in wingers with minimal to average goalscoring rates.

Or the ponderous nature of Arsenal's final-third entries when presented with a mid-block, or the general lack of life until Zigiotti Olme's opener reminded Slegers' side of the very real existence of their own jugular.

United's disciplined defence deserves plaudits, but Arsenal's failure to force United into any discomfort deserves scrutiny.

Since the start of last season, Arsenal's pressing intensity has trended downwards. A congested fixture schedule requires energy preservation, yet there was something discomfiting about a squad spoiled with pace and attacking hunger looking so tepid; almost apathetic to press United's back line, despite the joys both London City and Chelsea found when forcing Olid's team to play under any duress.

Instead, the final six minutes of added time painted a familiar scene: Arsenal desperate, shots snatched and blazed, potential penalty shouts pleaded for, and, in the end, a point critically salvaged, but faces contorted in frustration.

articles.title: Cowboys Rookie Turns Heads With On-Field ‘Double Puke’
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys' Jaishawn Barham had a huge play in the win over the Commanders. He left it all on the field in other ways, too. The post Cowboys Rookie T...
articles.body:
It was just the second game of the NFL career of Dallas Cowboys rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham , the team's third-round pick out of Michigan, and after some rough moments in his debut in New York last week, he came up with some big plays on Sunday in the 37-20 win over the Commanders . He had the biggest defensive play of the game with 7:15 to go in the third quarter, when he read a short screen pass to Dyami Brown and unloaded with a big hit just as Brown was making the catch. Brown fumbled to the Commanders' 13-yard line, setting up a touchdown that made a 20-13 lead 27-13.

That was not the only thing Barham was coughing up in the game, though. Just about three minutes after making the play on Brown, Barham was back at his linebacker spot and was seen on the Fox broadcast vomiting onto the field. Not once, but twice.

As one observer noted, "Jaishawn Barham with the pre-snap double-puke, which feels like a pretty good excuse to jog through the ensuing snap."

The clip of Barham made the rounds on social media, a surprise moment of–we think–nerves for a young Cowboys player who had handled himself well in the win.

Podcaster Tom Downey wrote , "Oh so this is why Jaishawn Barham didn't play as much in the 2nd half The old puke and puke again move."

Another observer noted, " Jaishawn Barham just threw up ALL over the field. Get that man some fluids ASAP!"

And another joked that Barham's bodily fluids were a signal to defenses. He wrote: "Did you notice the 'tell' with Cowboys LB Jaishawn Barham ? When he pukes, he drops back in coverage. When he doesn't puke , he's blitzing. I hope opposing teams don't pick up on this tendency."

Barham was a star of the preseason, and quickly worked his way up the Cowboys depth chart since the draft. He is one of the hardest hitters on the team, but he is still raw in many ways and still trying to polish up his game. But considering the weakness that the Cowboys have had in filling the linebacker hole in recent years, he has been a very solid find.

Defensive lineman Quinnen Williams spoke about Barham after Sunday's game.

"The plays he has been making are superdope, I have seen him make them in practice," Williams said. "I'm super-confident in him. Like I say, keep building on the things he do well, just like all of us, we got to keep building on the things we've got to correct. He played a great game. He played phenomenal. When it comes to wearing the green dot as a rookie, second game of the year, getting everybody in order, especially up front. Different things like that. Just continue to improve—we all have huge trust in him."

articles.title: Former Lions QB Calls Out Jared Goff During Rough Bills Loss
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions suffered their first loss of the 2026 NFL season in frustrating fashion on Thursday evening, falling behind by a 21-0 score to the host Buf...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions suffered their first loss of the 2026 NFL season in frustrating fashion on Thursday evening, falling behind by a 21-0 score to the host Buffalo Bills before eventually falling by a 41-31 final score.

The secondary of the Lions , who barely escaped what would have been a disastrous Week 1 loss against the New Orleans Saints days earlier at Ford Field, was carved up by Bills quarterback Josh Allen , who made his mark in the inaugural game at new Highmark Stadium with a vintage performance.

Speaking of quarterbacks, Jared Goff certainly can't be blamed for the loss – but he took a bit of heat from a key former Lion.

Former Detroit Lions Quarterback Dan Orlovsky Calls Out Current QB Jared Goff During Bills Loss

Former Lions backup quarterback Dan Orlovsky, now one of the best-known NFL Insiders, took Goff to task during the loss to the Bills for not targeting Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams more.

"Have like $100 million into (2) WRS and you've thrown them 2 balls… Bad ball," Orlovsky wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter.

It wouldn't be long before the replies began pouring in, with a good percentage of them seemingly agreeing.

One fan exclaimed , "He hasn't thrown it anyone!!! Throw the fucking ball Goff!!! On all days to take the over on 36.5 lol. He ends with ONE. ONE in the first quarter. ONE"

"Agreed but we also have no OL and Goff is cheeks without an OL this game never had a chance to be close once the injury report posted," one fan said.

This fan wanted to deflect blame to the Lions defense, saying , "Dan, at this point, you could close your laptop, and walk out on that field in your street clothes and throw for 400 against this Lions defense."

Another fan seemingly called out OC Drew Petzing, saying, "Goff is….. not very good. Dude is waiting for guys to be open. No anticipation, no throwing them open. Ben Johnson covered up a LOT of stink with him."

However, not all fans agreed with Orlovsky, with a few reminding him of the infamous moment during his own playing career that made blooper reels everywhere.

"YOU WANNA TALK ABOUT BAD DETROIT BALL, DAN-O?! Let's go back to October 12, 2008…" one fan said.

This fan said, "Having situational awareness so bad that you run out the back of the end zone…. Bad Ball."

Jared Goff Played Well Despite The Lions Loss

Goff had a strong game, completing 26-of-38 passes for 327 yards and four touchdowns and zero interceptions.

However, Detroit's porous secondary opened the door for a barrage of first-half points and yards for the Bills. Meanwhile, Goff took issue with what he felt was a lack of urgency during the first half.

"I think urgency early on," said Goff. "I think for the last two games, really, we had some good moments, but I think we need to understand that we need to start good; we need to start on that momentum. Those first two drives put us in a big hole, and we can't do that."

articles.title: Commanders’ Jayden Daniels Urged to Make Hard Change After Injury
articles.summary: It’s the second straight season in which Washington Commanders QB Jayden Daniels suffers an injury. In the 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, Daniels suffered...
articles.body:
It's the second straight season in which Washington Commanders QB Jayden Daniels suffers an injury. In the 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys , Daniels suffered a dislocated left elbow on the final play of the first half.

The Commanders star misstepped after taking the snap under center, bracing himself with his left arm before hitting the turf in obvious pain as his pass fell incomplete.

With another injury that will likely keep him out, CBS Sports' Ran Carthon believes Daniels is at a crossroads in his career and needs to focus on getting stronger to better withstand the physical demands of his playing style, or he risks continuing to suffer injuries.

"If you go back and listen to a lot of the drafting, people were like, at that size, I don't know if he's going to be able to hold up," Carthon said on Sept. 20 on "CBS Sports HQ." "Because he runs around, he uses his legs, which he did a good job of today, extending drives for [the Commanders].

"But both of those are non-contact or at least the one [against the Cowboys] where you just put it down, and this is where, hopefully, after this injury, because it looked pretty gruesome from our vantage point.

"This is where Jayden now has to take a step back and say, 'Hey, let me work on my body. Let me work on my body [and] let me bulk up. Let me get stronger.' Because the way he plays the game, he's always going to use that offhand to break his fall."

Jayden Daniels Told to Get Stronger After Latest Injury

Carthon continued to raise the question of whether Daniels can withstand the physical demands of playing quarterback while also being a threat as a runner.

"If you've now got to run the risk every time you're putting your hand down that your elbow is going to snap, that's going to play mentally in his head, but he's got to develop his body," Carthon added. "He's got to get stronger. He's got to add more weight on so he can withstand these types of things."

Commanders Give Jayden Daniels Update After Loss to Cowboys

Meanwhile, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told reporters X-rays did not show a fracture, but Daniels will travel back home with the team and undergo more imaging on Sept. 21.

"Once I know an update that we can move forward with, then I'll give you that," Quinn told reporters postgame (h/t NFL.com ). "Man, are we bummed for him. He was really playing his ass off. We will rally so hard around Marcus [ Mariota ] until Jayden's back. That's what we talked about as a team."

Before his injury, Daniels was 11 of 17 for 96 yards with a touchdown and also had 69 yards rushing on seven attempts, so once again his absence will be felt. Marcus Mariota started the second half for the Commanders in place of the injured Daniels, and Quinn mentioned that the veteran quarterback will take over under center for as long as Daniels is out.

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers ‘Have To Add’ WR Amid Significant Injuries
articles.summary: The 49ers’ battered receiver room took another hit Sunday, and Kyle Shanahan says a roster addition is now coming. The post San Francisco 49ers ‘Have To Add’...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers entered Week 2 with an increasingly thin wide receiver room. They left it with Kyle Shanahan acknowledging another move is coming.

After Demarcus Robinson exited San Francisco's 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins with an ankle injury on September 20, Shanahan was asked whether the 49ers would have to find another receiver.

His answer went considerably further than the standard promise to explore the market.

"I'm sure we'll have to add somebody," Shanahan said. "Whether it's the practice squad or to the roster, but those are things we'll start discussing tonight and hopefully have an answer by Wednesday."

The distinction matters. Shanahan did not guarantee San Francisco will sign an established free agent from outside the organization. He did, however, make clear that the 49ers expect to add another receiver in some form.

And at this point, necessity is driving the conversation.

Kyle Shanahan Says 49ers Will Discuss WR Addition Immediately

San Francisco has already lost Ricky Pearsall for the 2026 season after he underwent surgery to repair his right PCL. The team placed Pearsall on injured reserve in August, with general manager John Lynch saying his recovery could take between six and 12 months.

The 49ers placed the rookie second-round pick on injured reserve September 19 after ankle surgery. Shanahan previously said Stribling was expected to miss roughly 10 weeks.

Christian Kirk is also on injured reserve, although he was designated to return when San Francisco set its initial 53-man roster.

Shanahan said after the Miami game that Kirk still has "a couple weeks before he can come back."

Robinson's injury therefore created another problem at a position that was already operating without several anticipated contributors.

"That was big losing Stribling last week," Shanahan said. "You guys know how big it was losing Ricky over the summer. And then losing D-Rob today was huge."

San Francisco does have alternatives already in the building. KhaDarel Hodge was promoted to the active roster on September 16, while Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins were also listed among the receivers on the team's most recent depth chart.

But Shanahan's comments suggest the 49ers do not plan to simply stand pat.

Mike Evans Injury Update: Shanahan Says WR Could Have Returned

Mike Evans gave the 49ers another injury scare against Miami when he left with a hip issue.

That situation sounded considerably less concerning after the game.

Asked whether Evans had suffered a serious injury, Shanahan said he did not believe so.

"It can always change tomorrow, but I would have thought if the game was different, he would have been able to come back in," Shanahan said.

Evans had already made an impact before leaving. Brock Purdy found him for a 27-yard completion that took San Francisco to the Miami 1-yard line, one of Purdy's biggest throws during a 20-of-22, 287-yard performance.

That makes Robinson's status the more immediate concern.

Shanahan said Robinson's ankle injury "looked most likely like a high ankle sprain," while emphasizing that the team had not yet confirmed the diagnosis.

If that initial assessment holds, the 49ers could be without yet another receiver when they host the Arizona Cardinals on September 27.

The 49ers are 2-0 after convincing wins over the Los Angeles Rams and Dolphins. Their receiver depth, however, has been moving in the opposite direction.

Shanahan now expects them to do something about it.

articles.title: Colts vs Chiefs: Good, bad and ugly from overtime loss
articles.summary: Here is a look at the good, bad and ugly in the Indianapolis Colts' overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
articles.body:
It was a valiant effort with a lot of ups and downs for both teams, but the Indianapolis Colts ultimately fell short to the Kansas City Chiefs , losing 33-30 as time expired in overtime.

Quarterback Daniel Jones finished the game with 210 passing yards and a passing touchdown, while running back Jonathan Taylor was a bell cow for the Colts .

Taylor finished the game with 92 rushing yards, 40 receiving yards, and two touchdowns. However, on Indianapolis' drive in overtime, the Chiefs were prepared for Taylor in the red zone, stuffing him on back-to-back plays. That said, this game never would have gone to overtime if it were not for Taylor and his production.

Here is a look at the good, bad, and ugly in the Colts' overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs:

Jonathan Taylor: Taylor was the highlight of this game for Indianapolis. He served as the bell cow for the Colts throughout the entire game with 24 carries and four receptions. He also surpassed over 100 scrimmage yards for the second straight game. Taylor can always be counted on for reliable production throughout a game, and he is what makes this offense go.

Josh Downs : When Alec Pierce went down, Josh Downs stepped up as the leading receiver in this game. He did what the Colts needed of him. On his nine targets, he caught seven passes for 72 yards. With uncertainty around Pierce's status moving forward, Downs may have to take on a larger role for the time being.

Another early turnover: Daniel Jones did not have a bad game, and honestly, the interception was not his fault either. Maybe he could have placed the ball better to give Keenan Allen a better shot at it. Maybe he could have made a different read. But regardless, for the second consecutive game, the Colts followed up a scoring drive with a turnover, giving the opponent all the momentum.

Sauce Gardner 's dropped INT: This game could have been a lot different if Sauce Gardner had not dropped the interception from Patrick Mahomes . He jumped the route perfectly, and it hit him right in both hands. The drop proved costly as Kansas City would end up scoring a touchdown on that drive. When you have a chance at a momentum-changing turnover, you have to take it.

Pass Defense: The ugly in this game is pretty much just the defense. First, addressing the passing defense, Patrick Mahomes put up nearly 400 passing yards and three touchdowns. This is the second game in a row Indianapolis has allowed a quarterback to have at least 300 passing yards against them. This is also the second week they allowed a 100-yard receiver, giving up 150 yards to Zay Flowers in the opener and 101 yards to Travis Kelce in this game. Indianapolis is going to lose a lot of games if they keep giving up these kinds of numbers.

Run Defense: Derrick Henry had 144 rushing yards against them in the opener, with Baltimore topping 200 rushing yards as a team. Kansas City did not quite get to 200 rushing yards, but their leading running back Kenneth Walker III had 117 rushing yards, including 18 rushing yards and 22 passing yards on the final drive of the game. Indianapolis is not going to go far, giving up a 100-yard receiver and a 100-yard rusher in every game.

articles.title: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. ‘Embarrassed’ by Poor Season for Blue Jays
articles.summary: According to a prominent Canadian sports writer, Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is “embarrassed” by his poor season.Guerrero is enduri...
articles.body:
According to a prominent Canadian sports writer, Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is "embarrassed" by his poor season.

Guerrero is enduring the worst season of his eight-year MLB career so far.

The six-time MLB All-Star is batting just .262 for the Blue Jays with an OPS of .694 and an OPS+ of 92, indicating his bat has been 8% below league average. He has only hit 9 home runs this season, including just 1 home run at Rogers Centre.

Considering Guerrero makes $40.2 million this season, the first year of a 14-year, $500 million contract, it has been downright shocking, to say the least, to see how poorly he has performed at the plate this year for Toronto , which is likely to miss the postseason after making it all the way to the World Series last year, in what can only be described as a massive fall from grace.

Vladimir Guerrero Jr. 'Embarrassed' by Poor Performance

According to Steve Simmons of the Toronto Sun , Guerrero has told those close to him that he is "embarrassed" by his play this season.

"Those who know Guerrero best say he is terribly embarrassed by his lack of production and he has grown tired of all the meetings, the coaching, the daily work, the noise that has not resulted in anything resembling success during this wayward season," Simmons wrote.

Simmons also provided another interesting note, pointing out that in the event of an MLB lockout — which seems likely at this point — Guerrero will not be able to work with the Blue Jays coaches after December 1 to help get his swing back on track this offseason.

"What complicates the off-season for Guerrero and the Jays is the possibility of a lockout on Dec. 1. If that happens, and the Jays have plans to work with Guerrero to get his swing back, there can be no contact between the player and the team after that date," Simmons wrote.

With just six games left this season, the Blue Jays have a 77-79 record, and making the postseason is going to be next to impossible, as the team is currently 3 GB of the Chicago White Sox in the hunt for the third and final American League Wild Card spot.

That's actually 4 GB, though, because the White Sox hold the tiebreaker over Toronto, so the odds of the Blue Jays making it to the postseason bracket are extremely slim right now.

The only hope Toronto has is that they win their last six games of the season to get to 83-79 and hope that Chicago goes 2-4 in their last six games to finish at 82-80.

Or, the Cleveland Guardians can go 2-4 over their final six games to also finish at 83-79, as Toronto at least has the tiebreaker over Cleveland.

With that in mind, math is not on the Blue Jays' side right now, as time is running out this season and there simply aren't enough games left for Toronto to get into the postseason bracket.

And fairly or unfairly, since it is a team sport, Guerrero's bad season with the bat is a big reason why the team isn't going anywhere this year.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Injury Update Gives Commanders Relief Ahead of Week 3
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels opened 2026 with a chance to move past an injury-filled 2025. The Washington Commanders quarterback showed flashes in Week 1, throwing two tou...
articles.body:
Jayden Daniels opened 2026 with a chance to move past an injury-filled 2025. The Washington Commanders quarterback showed flashes in Week 1, throwing two touchdowns in a 24-22 road loss to the Philadelphia Eagles . A week later, Sunday's trip to Dallas became a different kind of test. Washington now waits on medical news that could shape the next several weeks of its season.

Jayden Daniels Avoids Fracture After Elbow Dislocation

Good news arrived Sunday night for Washington. NFL insider Adam Schefter reported that X-rays on Jayden Daniels' left elbow showed no fracture. The update came after a 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys , when head coach Dan Quinn spoke to reporters.

The injury came on the final play of the first half. Daniels took an under-center snap on third-and-goal from the 1-yard line, and left guard Chris Paul appeared to step on his feet. Daniels tried to brace his fall with his left arm, and the elbow bent back. Trainers reached him quickly, and he was carted off with an air cast on the arm.

"He did injure his left elbow, it was a dislocation," Quinn said afterward.

Daniels will travel home with the team for more imaging Monday. Quinn also said he expects the quarterback to return this season.

Before the injury, Daniels had completed 11 of 17 passes for 96 yards and a touchdown. He also ran seven times for 69 yards. Marcus Mariota took over at quarterback for the second half.

The bigger question is how this scare compares with the elbow injury that derailed his 2025 season.

Daniels now revisits an injury that cost him last season

Daniels dislocated the same left elbow on Nov. 2, 2025, in a Week 9 loss to the Seattle Seahawks . An MRI found no fracture or ligament damage, so he avoided surgery and stayed off injured reserve.

He missed several games, returned in Week 14 against the Minnesota Vikings , and aggravated the elbow again. Washington then shut him down for the final three weeks to protect his recovery. He finished 2025 with only seven games played.

Expectations were high heading into this season, and an ESPN expert pointed to the hype around Daniels.

The moment hit teammates hard. Running back Rachaad White , a longtime friend of Daniels, was emotional.

"I tried to control my emotions, but I had tears coming down," White told reporters.

Now, Washington sits at 0-2 and expects Marcus Mariota to lead the offense while Daniels recovers. The Commanders host the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on Sept. 27. Seattle opened 2026 with a win over New England , so the test looks steep.

articles.summary: Woody Marks turned 13 opportunities into only 35 yards in Week 2 vs. the Bengals.
articles.body:
Houston Texans RB Woody Marks carried eight times for eight yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in a Week 2 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals .

articles.body:
EVANSVILLE, Ind. (WEHT) - It took all five games, but the Otters finally moved past the Washington Wild Things and win the conference finals three games to two.

Sunday was a must win for the Evansville and they won it 9-6.

Logan Brown started things with a solo shot in the 2nd and then the offense scored five more in the next inning.

LG Castillo had a two-run bomb in that inning to give Evansville a six-run cushion.

Otters tacked on two more in the 6th inning.

They will now play the Ottawa Titans in the Frontier League Championship series.

Games 1&2 will be right here in Evansville on Tuesday and Wednesday.

This is the second time in four years that the championship series returns to Bosse Field.

It will be a best-of-five series for the championship.

articles.title: Dalton Schultz the lone offensive star for Houston in Week 2
articles.summary: Dalton Schultz goes off for 12 catches and 140 yards in Week 2 home loss against Cincinnati.
articles.body:
Houston Texans TE Dalton Schultz caught 12 of 14 targets for 140 yards in a Week 2 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals .

Why It Matters: Schultz posted career highs in receptions, targets and yards; his previous highs were 10 grabs, 11 targets and 130 yards – all in 2023 for Houston against Tampa Bay in Week 9. This was Schultz's second career 100-plus yard performance. Usually a TE2 option when Nico Collins is healthy, Schultz will certainly draw attention on the waiver wire this week and could be treated as a low-end TE1 in Week 3 versus the Colts .
